prompt: A new, original scene in the same pixel-art style as the reference, from the high three-quarter, top-down camera of a cosy farming game. The first morning on an overgrown, unbuilt plot of land that someone has just arrived to make their own: tall wild grass, weeds and wildflowers, scattered stones, two old tree stumps, fallen branches, a collapsed stretch of old split-rail fence, a few young trees at the edges. In the middle, a small clearing where work has just begun: four freshly tilled squares of dark soil, a hoe and a watering can leaning against a stump, a blank wooden signpost with no writing on it, a stack of fresh timber beside a few corner stakes and string marking out where a first building might go, and a dirt path leading in from the bottom edge. Full of possibility: everything is still to be decided. The plot is an isolated, roughly rectangular island of ground with soft natural edges on a transparent background, with nothing outside it. Pixel art with the polish of a lovingly hand-made indie game: drawn on a native canvas of 384 by 256 art pixels, every art pixel exactly 4 by 4 screen pixels on one strict, even grid, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients. One-art-pixel dark outlines that are consistent everywhere, hand-placed dithering only in shadows, readable silhouettes, and a small cohesive palette of about 24 warm colors. Small lived-in details reward a second look. Palette: grass and sage greens, warm earth browns, honey wood, cream, warm greys, near-black ink (#1C1A17) outlines, and a single burnt-orange accent (#B84A16) on one or two small details such as the watering can. Calm, warm, hopeful. No people, no animals, no text or letters anywhere, no logos, no user interface, no robots, no glowing brains, no sparkles, no stars.
